issues.legal_issue: A certified copy of a registered sale deed may be admitted as secondary evidence to prove the contents of the original under the Evidence Act and Registration Act.

A certified copy of a registered sale deed admissible under the applicable statutory provisions does not require proof through an independent witness or recourse to the presumptions under Sections 90 and 110 of the Evidence Act.
A High Court may interfere with concurrent findings of fact in a second appeal only where a substantial question of law justifies interference under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

A purchaser who establishes the vendor’s title and the transfer of the entire described property is entitled to title and possession over that entire property, absent proof of a superior competing title.
